name: Mchwatox 350 SC Termiticide
lead: Termites work out of sight. They tunnel through the soil, reach a building at the foundation and can weaken doors, frames and roof timbers before anyone sees a sign. Mchwatox 350 SC is a suspension concentrate (SC) termiticide containing imidacloprid 350 g/L, supplied in a 1 litre bottle. It is used for soil treatment against termites in buildings and construction, both before a building goes up (pre-construction) and on buildings that already stand (post-construction).
features: Suspension concentrate (SC) termiticide
Active ingredient: imidacloprid 350 g/L
Pre-construction soil treatment, before the slab or foundation is laid
Post-construction treatment of existing buildings
Used around foundations, trenches and building perimeters as the label directs
1 litre bottle
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Dilution and spray volume: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: Termite damage to timber, roofing, doors, frames, fences and furniture is costly to repair once it shows. Treating the soil around and under a building is one way to build a protective barrier, applied at construction stage and repeated or topped up where termites appear later. Mchwatox 350 SC is made for this soil-treatment job, so it suits builders, contractors, pest control operators and property owners.
use: Start with an inspection to find where termites enter and where they nest. Dilute Mchwatox 350 SC with water exactly as the label directs, and apply it thoroughly and evenly to the soil, using the dilution and the volume of spray liquid printed on the label. For a new building the treatment goes on before the slab or foundation is laid. For an existing building it is applied around the foundations, trenches and perimeter as the label describes.
before: Fix leaking pipes and damp areas that keep the soil wet
Remove old tree stumps and buried timber near the building
Keep timber and firewood from direct contact with the soil
For a large building, consider a licensed pest control operator
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear gloves, a mask, overalls and boots, avoid contact with skin and eyes, and keep the product away from children, pets, food, water sources and fish ponds. Do not contaminate wells, boreholes or drains when you mix, spray or wash equipment.
storage: Keep Mchwatox 350 SC in its original, tightly closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and direct sunlight.
faq: What is Mchwatox 350 SC used for?
It is a termiticide for soil treatment against termites in buildings and construction, both before building (pre-construction) and on existing buildings (post-construction).
What is the active ingredient?
Imidacloprid at 350 g/L, formulated as a suspension concentrate (SC). The exact strength and registration details are printed on the label.
Should I hire a professional to apply it?
For a large building, a licensed pest control operator is a sensible choice. Whoever applies it must follow the label for dilution, spray volume and safety.

name: Metro 200SC Termiticide
lead: Subterranean termites live in the soil and travel through tunnels to reach fence posts, roof members and other wooden structures. Metro 200SC is a suspension concentrate (SC) termiticide containing imidacloprid 200 g/L, used for soil treatment against subterranean termites. It comes in a small 25 ml pack, a practical choice for homeowners, small construction jobs, wooden posts and fences.
features: Non-repellent, odourless and colourless termiticide
Active ingredient: imidacloprid 200 g/L
For soil treatment, timber, posts and wooden fences
Termites do not easily detect and avoid the treated area
Leaves no strong smell in the home or compound
Small 25 ml pack that is easy to store and handle
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Dilution: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: A soil treatment places a protective zone between the termites and the structure you want to protect. Because Metro 200SC is non-repellent, odourless and colourless, termites do not easily detect and avoid the treated area, and nothing smells strongly in your home or compound. It suits soil treatment around small structures and the base of fence posts and timber before they go into the ground.
use: Find the termite activity first: look for mud tubes on walls, hollow-sounding timber and soil mounds nearby. Then treat the soil thoroughly as directed on the label, and treat the base of fence posts and timber before they are placed in the ground. The label gives the dilution. A 25 ml pack is small, so measure carefully and mix only what the job needs.
before: Remove rotting wood and tree stumps close to your building
Repair leaks that keep the ground damp
Keep firewood and stored timber off the ground
For a whole building or a large infestation, consider a licensed pest control operator
safety: Check the PCPB registration number on the label, and mix and apply exactly as directed. Wear protective gear, keep Metro 200SC away from children, pets, food and water, and never contaminate water sources when you mix or spray.
storage: Keep the 25 ml pack tightly closed in its original container, in a cool, dry place out of reach of children and away from food.
faq: What is Metro 200SC used for?
It is used for soil treatment against subterranean termites, and for the base of timber, fence posts and wooden fences.
Will it leave a smell or a stain?
Metro 200SC is described as odourless and colourless, so it leaves no strong smell in your home or compound.
Can I treat a whole building with the 25 ml pack?
The pack suits homeowners, small construction jobs, posts and fences. For a whole building or a large infestation, consider a licensed pest control operator.

name: Premise 200 SC Termiticide
lead: Termites (mchwa) rarely announce themselves. They eat door frames, roof timbers and cupboards from the inside until the damage is expensive. Bayer Premise 200 SC is a non-repellent, odourless termiticide with imidacloprid 200 g/L. Termites walk through the treated soil without detecting it, carry the active ingredient back and spread it through the colony.
features: Non-repellent with a transfer effect, so it reaches termites you cannot see
Suitable for pre-construction and post-construction treatment
Also listed for controlling ants
Practically odourless at the recommended dilution
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Applications: foundations, slab preparation, trenches, termite mounds and wall voids
helps: It suits a builder treating hardcore and soil before the slab is cast, a homeowner treating the foundation lines of an existing house, and anyone dealing with a termite mound or wall void.
dose: Dilution: 50 ml Premise 200 SC per 20 L knapsack of water (0.25%)
Application volume: 5 L of mixed solution per m² of soil, or per linear metre of trench along foundations
One knapsack covers about 4 m² or 4 linear metres
A 1 litre bottle mixes 20 knapsacks (400 L), enough for about 80 m² or 80 linear metres
use: Shake the bottle vigorously, half fill the knapsack with clean water, add the measured Premise, top up to 20 L and stir. Pre-construction: treat the hardcore and soil before the slab is cast. Trenches: apply along the inside and outside of the foundation lines. Existing buildings: drill and inject along foundations and slab joints, and for a mound, drill into the nest and drench it thoroughly. Do not apply in rain or when rain is expected, and wash all equipment after use. Check the rates against the label on your pack.
before: Fix leaks and remove old stumps and buried timber near the building
Keep treated soil away from wells, boreholes and drains
For a large building, consider a licensed pest control operator
safety: Harmful. Wear gloves, overalls, boots and a mask when mixing and spraying. It is toxic to bees and aquatic life, so never let spray or wash water reach streams, ponds, wells or drains.
storage: Store the unused product in its original, closed pack in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and children.
faq: How does Premise 200 SC kill the whole colony?
It is non-repellent, so termites cross the treated soil without detecting it. They carry the active ingredient back and spread it through the colony.
How much does one knapsack of Premise cover?
Mixed at 50 ml per 20 L and applied at 5 L per m², one knapsack treats about 4 m² of soil or 4 linear metres of trench. Confirm the rates on your label.
Which pack should I choose, 50 ml or 1 litre?
The 50 ml pack makes one 20 L knapsack, which suits a small job. The 1 litre bottle makes twenty, which suits a house or a building site.

name: Actellic 25EC Insecticide
lead: Insects in a store do their damage quietly, and by the time you notice them, stored produce can already be spoiled. Actellic 25EC is an emulsifiable concentrate (EC) insecticide containing pirimiphos-methyl, supplied in a 1 litre bottle for pest control in stores and premises. It is a professional pack for farms, grain stores, warehouses and other premises where insects need to be kept under control.
features: Emulsifiable concentrate (EC) that mixes with water for spraying
Active ingredient: pirimiphos-methyl, with the strength printed on the label
1 litre professional pack for stores and premises
Actellic brand product
For farms, grain stores, warehouses and similar premises
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Active ingredient: pirimiphos-methyl (strength on the label)
Dilution: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: Crawling and flying insects gather in stores, warehouses and farm buildings, and stored produce suffers when they settle in. Actellic 25EC is sprayed on the surfaces of empty stores, warehouses and other premises before stock goes in, and in places where those insects gather. It suits farmers preparing a store before harvest, traders and aggregators who hold produce, estate managers and institutions that keep food and feed, and pest control operators who want a larger refill pack.
use: As an emulsifiable concentrate, Actellic 25EC is diluted with water as directed on the label and applied as a spray. Follow the label for the correct dilution, the surfaces to treat and any waiting period before food, feed or people return to the area. Allow surfaces to dry as the label directs before storing grain or other produce, and stack new stock off the floor and away from the walls so that air can move and you can inspect it easily.
before: Sweep out old grain and dust
Repair cracks and holes where insects hide
Remove spilled produce before spraying
Clean sacks, pallets and containers, because old residues carry pests from one season to the next
Use a sprayer that is kept for pesticides only
safety: Read and follow the label before use. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when mixing and spraying, and wash your hands and face afterwards. Keep it away from children, pets, food and water, do not contaminate food, feed, streams or ponds, and never reuse the empty bottle.
storage: Keep Actellic 25EC in the original, tightly closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food, feed and direct sunlight.
faq: What is Actellic 25EC used for?
It is used for pest control in stores and premises, such as empty grain stores and warehouses before stock goes in.
How do I mix it?
Dilute it with water exactly as the label directs. Do not guess the rate.
Is Actellic 25EC the same as Actellic 50EC?
No. They are separate products with their own labels and dilution rates, so never use the rate for one on the other.

name: Actellic 50EC Insecticide
lead: Weevils and moths can turn a full store of maize into dust within months. Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate emulsifiable concentrate with pirimiphos-methyl 500 g/L. It acts by contact, ingestion and fumigant action, and it keeps working on walls, floors and bag surfaces after you spray.
features: Controls weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps
Acts by contact, ingestion and fumigant action
Keeps working on treated walls, floors and bag surfaces
Three uses: store surface spray, bagged grain and grain admixture
specs: Pack sizes: 100 ml, 250 ml, 500 ml, 1 litre
helps: Insects arrive with the harvest and hide in cracks, on walls and on bag surfaces, so the building needs treating as well as the grain. Actellic 50EC covers three jobs: surface spraying of stores and livestock houses, treating bagged grain, and mixing into stored grain as an admixture.
dose: Walls, floors, empty stores and livestock houses: 100 ml in 10 L of water (200 ml per 20 L knapsack)
Bagged grain and bag stacks: 50 to 100 ml in 5 L of water per 100 m² (200 to 400 ml per 20 L knapsack). Use the higher end for an existing infestation
Admixture to stored grain: 8 ml per tonne of grain, diluted in 0.75 to 1.5 L of water (not mixed in the knapsack)
Coverage: about 5 L of spray per 100 m². Porous surfaces such as concrete, brick and unpainted wood may need up to 15 L per 100 m²
One 20 L tank covers roughly 400 m² on normal surfaces and about 130 m² on porous ones
use: Clean and sweep the store first, removing old grain and debris, then spray to wet all surfaces without run-off. For admixture, dilute the measured amount in the water volume shown and apply it to the grain, not in the knapsack. These are the rates the catalog already published for this product, so check them against the label on your pack before mixing. Do not use Actellic 50EC with thermal foggers.
before: Remove food, feed and animals before spraying
Ventilate the store afterwards
Measure the area first, so that you mix only the volume you need
safety: Actellic 50EC is an organophosphate, so wear gloves, a mask and overalls when mixing and spraying, and keep children, pets, food, feed and water away. Label grain treated by admixture as chemically treated, and follow any waiting period on the pack.
storage: Store the bottle closed, in its original container, in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.
faq: Which pests does Actellic 50EC control?
The catalog lists weevils, beetles, moths, flies and wasps.
Can I use Actellic 50EC in a thermal fogger?
No. The catalog advice for this product is not to use it with thermal foggers.
How much does one 20 L knapsack cover?
About 400 m² on normal surfaces and roughly 130 m² on porous ones such as concrete, brick and unpainted wood.

name: Actellic Gold Dust
lead: Actellic Gold Dust is a ready-to-use dust for protecting stored grain from insect damage. It combines pirimiphos-methyl (16 g/kg) and thiamethoxam (3.6 g/kg) in a dustable powder, and it is registered in Kenya by the Pest Control Products Board (PCPB(CR) 1149). The 100 g, 500 g and 1 kg packs suit households and small farms storing maize and other cereals.
features: Ready to use, with no mixing in water
Two active ingredients working together against stored-grain pests
Registered in Kenya by the Pest Control Products Board
Three pack sizes: 100 g, 500 g and 1 kg
Suits household and small farm storage
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Active ingredients: pirimiphos-methyl 16 g/kg and thiamethoxam 3.6 g/kg
helps: The catalog lists the larger grain borer, grain weevil, red flour beetle, lesser grain borer and other stored-grain beetles and moths. These pests can ruin a harvest in a few months, hollowing out kernels, leaving dust and spoiling grain for food, seed and sale. A dust that goes in as the grain is stored keeps working inside the bag.
dose: About 50 g per 90 kg of grain, the size of a standard bag, as printed on the pack
Mix the dust evenly through the grain as it goes into storage
Do not use more than the label directs
use: Mix the dust evenly through the grain as it goes into storage. At the pack rate of about 50 g per 90 kg bag, a 100 g pack treats about two bags, a 500 g pack about ten and a 1 kg pack about twenty. Even mixing matters, because pests survive in untreated pockets, so turn the grain until the dust is spread through every bag. Follow the label exactly.
before: Clean and dry the store, and use dry, clean bags
Remove old grain, sweep out dust and fix cracks where insects can hide
Make sure the grain is properly dry before storing, because damp grain spoils even when treated
safety: Avoid breathing the dust, and wear a mask and gloves when mixing. Keep it away from children, pets and food, and wash your hands afterwards. Follow the label's waiting period before using treated grain, and do not rinse containers into water sources.
storage: Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry place out of reach of children.
faq: What does Actellic Gold Dust protect against?
Stored-grain pests such as the larger grain borer, grain weevil, red flour beetle and lesser grain borer, and other stored-grain beetles and moths.
Do I mix it with water?
No. It is a ready-to-use dust that is mixed evenly through the grain as it goes into storage.
How much should I use?
The pack rate is about 50 g per 90 kg of grain, the size of a standard bag. Follow the label exactly and do not use more than directed.
Is it registered in Kenya?
The catalog lists the Pest Control Products Board registration PCPB(CR) 1149. Check the number on your pack.

name: Grain-Save Dust
lead: Grain-Save Dust is a permethrin-based protectant for stored maize and beans against weevils and other storage pests. It is mixed into dry grain at the rate printed on the label and comes in a 500 g pack suited to farmers and households storing grain.
features: Permethrin-based dust
Protects stored maize and beans
Works against weevils and other storage pests
Mixed into dry grain at the label rate
500 g pack
Delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Active ingredient: permethrin (strength on the label)
Use: grain protectant for stored maize and beans
Rate: as printed on the manufacturer's label
helps: After harvest, weevils can hollow out kernels, leave dust and holes, lower germination and make grain unfit for food or sale. Losses can be heavy within a few months, especially in warm, humid stores. Treating grain as it goes into storage protects the work you put into the crop and keeps seed and food grain in good condition for longer.
use: Make sure the grain is properly dry before storage, because damp grain spoils even when treated. Mix the dust into the dry grain at the label rate, turning the grain thoroughly so the dust is spread evenly through every bag or heap. Even mixing is important, because untreated pockets let pests survive. Put the treated grain into clean, dry bags or containers, and store it off the ground and away from walls.
before: Sweep out old grain and dust, and repair cracks and holes
Use clean, dry bags and keep the store dry and well ventilated
Do not use it on grain that has already been treated, because two protectants on the same grain can leave too much residue
Check stored grain regularly for live insects, holes and powdery dust
safety: Read the label before use. Wear a mask, gloves and protective clothing when mixing, and avoid breathing the dust. Follow the label's waiting period before using treated grain, and do not feed treated grain to animals unless the label allows it. Permethrin is very toxic to fish, so never rinse containers or equipment into streams, ponds or drains.
storage: Keep the pack closed in a cool, dry, locked place away from food and feed.
faq: What is Grain-Save Dust used for?
It protects stored maize and beans against weevils and other storage pests.
Can I add it to grain that was already treated?
No. Using two protectants on the same grain can leave too much residue. If you are not sure whether your grain has been treated, do not add more.
Can I feed treated grain to animals?
Not unless the label allows it. Read the label for the waiting period and for any limits on feed use.

name: Thermal Fogging Machine Pulsed Power Sprayer
lead: Mosquitoes, flies and other pests hide in corners and crevices that a hand sprayer reaches slowly. The Thermal Fogging Machine Pulsed Power Sprayer is a professional pulse thermal fogger for mosquito, fly and pest control and fumigation. It is built with durable dual tanks and stainless steel heat pipes, and it is sold as a single unit for farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas.
features: Professional pulse thermal fogger for mosquito, fly and pest control
Durable dual tanks
Stainless steel heat pipes
Fast, efficient fog distribution that reaches all crevices and corners
For farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas
Sold as 1 unit and delivered to all 47 counties
specs: Product: Thermal Fogging Machine Pulsed Power Sprayer
Uses: mosquito, fly and pest control and fumigation
Suited to: farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas
Fuel type, tank capacity and output: see the manufacturer's manual (not listed in our catalog)
helps: A fog spreads through a space, which is why fogging is used where pests hide in cracks and corners. This machine is the equipment, not the insecticide, so you pair it with a product whose label allows thermal fogging and follow that label for the amount to use.
use: The catalog does not give the fuel, tank capacity or settings, so follow the manufacturer's manual for filling, start-up and shut-down. Before you fill a tank, read the insecticide label to confirm the product may be used in a thermal fogger, and follow its dilution and the time the space must stay closed. For example, the catalog advice for Actellic 50EC says it must not be used with thermal foggers. Treat only the space you have prepared, and let the machine cool before you handle or move it.
before: Read the machine manual and the insecticide label before the first use
Remove people, pets, food, feed and animals from the space
Keep flammable materials away from the machine and its hot parts
safety: A thermal fogger gets hot, so never touch the heat pipes while the machine is running or cooling. Wear the protective equipment named on the insecticide label, including a respirator if the label requires one, and do not enter a fogged space until the label says it is safe to do so. Keep the machine away from children.
storage: Let the machine cool completely, empty the tanks as the manual directs, and store it dry and out of reach of children, away from food and feed.
faq: What is the Thermal Fogging Machine used for?
It is a pulse thermal fogger for mosquito, fly and pest control and fumigation on farms, in greenhouses and warehouses, and in residential areas.
Which insecticide goes in the tanks?
The catalog does not name one. Choose a product whose label allows thermal fogging and follow its dilution. For example, the catalog advice for Actellic 50EC is not to use it with thermal foggers.
Where can I use it?
The catalog lists farms, greenhouses, warehouses and residential areas.
